nary_nodes.label: Victory parade in Madrid
evidence: Spain's newly crowned World Cup champions were greeted by a million fans as the team arrived for the victory parade in Madrid.

The players, some shirtless, others holding drinks, set off on their procession along the main arteries in the city centre where a sea of fans in red and yellow were waiting, with the destination Cibeles square.

nary_nodes.label: World Cup final victory
evidence: Spain's 1-0 victory over Argentina in New Jersey on Sunday, secured by a Ferran Torres strike in extra-time, has sparked an outpouring of national pride in the football-mad country, whose only other World Cup triumph came in 2010.

nary_nodes.label: Royal reception
evidence: After flying back from the United States to Madrid, the players were received by King Felipe VI and the royal family, and then Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, before kicking off the parade.

nary_nodes.label: Flight back to Madrid
evidence: After flying back from the United States to Madrid, the players were received by King Felipe VI and the royal family, and then Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, before kicking off the parade.

nary_nodes.label: Fans celebrate in Madrid
evidence: On Monday morning, the Castellana, Madrid's main avenue, bore the marks of a boozy evening – the tarmac strewn with trash, beer cans and shards of glass.

Among the last remaining supporters, some slept with grins on their faces on the pavement or on benches, while others were still staggering home as cleaning crews worked from the early hours to prepare the route for tonight's party.

nary_nodes.label: Boy killed in fountain collapse
evidence: On a tragic note, a 13-year-old boy was killed around midnight in the town of Ciudad Rodrigo in the west, after a fountain crumbled under the weight of supporters who had climbed onto it to celebrate.

nary_nodes.label: Women's World Cup win
evidence: Spain’s women’s side won the World Cup in 2023, meaning for the first time a country has both trophies at the same time.

nary_nodes.label: Defend crown in 2030
evidence: In 2030, Spain will defend their crown on home soil, as one of the World Cup hosts along with Portugal and Morocco.

nary_nodes.label: Semi-final victory over France
evidence: The Spanish press was running out of superlatives to describe its heroes after they overcame favourites France in the semi-finals before downing Argentina.

nary_nodes.label: King praises team
evidence: “You have shown your grit, your resilience and your courage, always backed by your technical skill, your control and command of the game, combining head and heart,” the king told La Roja’s stars.

nary_nodes.label: Rodri's career highlight
evidence: Later at Moncloa, the Manchester City midfielder said this was the crowning achievement of his career.
“I’ve always said it, winning with your country is the most beautiful thing there is, above all a World Cup,” said Rodri.
“This generation grew up watching (Iker) Casillas and (Andres) Iniesta lift the cup and that we can do it today is the biggest thing you can do in football.”

nary_nodes.label: Sanchez dreams of third title
evidence: “It’s two for two,” said Sanchez, of Spain’s record in World Cup finals. “Why not dream of a third in 2030, especially with Spain as hosts?”

nary_nodes.label: Messi's pain
evidence: “The pain is immense, and it’s going to be hard for this wound to heal,” Messi wrote on Instagram.
